title: Special Topics - Neuroethology
description: Students study different animal models, ranging from insects and amphibians to birds and mammals, to learn about their specialized behaviors and the neural circuitries that govern them. The goal of this classic branch of behavioral neuroscience is to understand how the nervous system encodes relevant natural stimuli to trigger an appropriate behavioral response. By studying some of the evolutionarily robust behaviors, we can begin to uncover some shared fundamental principles of the nervous system.

title: Advanced Topics in Human Behavioral Endocrinology
description: This course focuses on developing functional accounts of the roles of hormones in human psychology and behavior. Existing hormone research commonly neglects functional explanations and instead attempts to develop parsimonious descriptions of the general effects of specific hormones. Uses published findings to develop and critically evaluate models of how hormones act as signals that prime functional output responses to the eliciting conditions that trigger hormone release. This exercise could be applied to research on human estradiol and progesterone, testosterone, cortisol, and oxytocin, but there is flexibility in the specific topics emphasized depending on the interests of students enrolled in the class.

title: The Social Mind of Primates
description: Humans possess many unique psychological capacities for navigating our social worlds, but we also share extensive sociocognitive similarities with other primates. In this course, we explore the origins and trajectories of primate social minds through comparative and evolutionary frameworks.

title: Contemporary Issues in Biopsychology - Systems Neuroscience
description: Presentation and discussion of current research in systems neuroscience. Focus on how neural circuits mediate specific behaviors, drawing on research from a range of species and preparations. Also serves as an introduction to the methodological approaches used in systems neuroscience, including electrophysiology, cellular imaging, and optogenetics.

title: Animal Models of Neuropsychiatric Disorders
description: Animal models are important tools in the study of psychiatric disorders, but what is a "good" animal model of a psychiatric disorder? In this course, we examine how animal models are generated, discuss their validity and utility in neuropsychiatric research, and review some of the major neuroscientific insights made possible by animal models. Topics may include: Depression, Addiction, Schizophrenia, Autism, PTSD, OCD

title: Neuroscience of Motivation
description: Retraces the history of our understanding of motivated behaviors, from the early psychological and neuroscientific studies to the modern day. We examine how coordinated activity within specific neural circuits mediates specific psychological components of motivation. Topics may include: consummatory behaviors, appetitive behaviors, pleasure, decision-making.
